title: Ruff v. Nashville Presbytery
disposition_detail: Adopted SJC decision: complaint judicially out of order under OMSJC 10.5.a.; case dismissed under OMSJC 10.6 because the filing defect could not be cured. The SJC held BCO 43-1 requires an act or decision, and that a court's “lack of action” can be treated as a decision only when there is a meeting of the court at which it fails to act; BCO 43-2's thirty days therefore ran from Nashville Presbytery's August 18, 2010 meeting, making the October 27, 2010 complaint late. No merits ruling. RE Samuel J. Duncan's objection is not an adopted disposition.
first_summary: The SJC dismissed Matt Ruff's complaint against Nashville Presbytery because it was filed more than thirty days after Presbytery's August 18, 2010 meeting. Ruff complained that Presbytery failed to act on his request to investigate a teaching elder. The adopted ruling treated that lack of action as a court decision only if a meeting was pending, so the October 27 filing was late. The merits of the underlying investigation request were not reached.
summary: The SJC dismissed Matt Ruff's complaint against Nashville Presbytery as judicially out of order under OMSJC 10.5.a. Ruff challenged Presbytery's failure to investigate a teaching elder, but BCO 43 requires a complaint against an act or decision; lack of action qualifies only when a court meeting has occurred and the court failed to act. Presbytery's nearest antecedent meeting was August 18, 2010, and Ruff filed October 27, 2010, beyond BCO 43-2's thirty-day limit. Because the defect could not be cured, the case was dismissed without reaching the merits; a separate objection disputed that ruling.

sources.supports: Identity, adopted disposition and reasons, roll call, and separate objection.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: Lines 1–5, 11–13, 33–38: SJC case 2010-27; decision drafted by TE David Coffin and adopted as the decision of the full SJC; roll call shows 18 concurring, 1 disqualified, and 5 absent (printed pp. 538–540).
evidence_notes.dispute: Lines 21–29 and 78–88: Ruff filed an October 27, 2010 complaint against Nashville Presbytery's failure to act on his request concerning a second teaching elder; the objection recounts the July 9, 2008 letter and the November 9, 2010 presbytery denial.
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: Lines 13–31: adopted holding that the complaint is judicially out of order and the case dismissed; reasons are BCO 43-1/43-2 and OMSJC 10.5.a/10.6; nearest presbytery meeting was August 18, 2010, making the October 27, 2010 filing late.
evidence_notes.qualifications: Lines 69–108: RE Samuel J. Duncan filed an objection disputing the judicial out-of-order ruling and arguing BCO 39-3.1, waiver/estoppel, and unfairness; it is a separate objection, not the adopted decision. Lines 33–34 note Ruff's standing based on SJC case 2009-28.
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: Adopted footnote cites SJC case 2009-28 only for Ruff's standing (lines 33–34); the objection references SJC case 2010-26 (lines 104–106), but that reference is not adopted. No adopted decision is incorporated by reference with an unavailable result.

source_limits: The source contains the adopted SJC decision, roll call, and one objection, but no full lower-court record, transcript, or adopted merits findings. Nashville Presbytery's November 9, 2010 denial appears only in the objector's factual account.
